power.connection: Supply positive to Pico 2 VSYS, supply return to Pico 2 GND; never connect supply positive to VBUS or micro-USB.
stopConditions: Any voltage appears on the disconnected micro-USB VBUS pin.
The supply enters current limit during a no-load or normal-idle test.
Any cable, probe ground, display pin or UART VCC creates an unreviewed second power path.
VSYS exceeds 5.5V or any GPIO exceeds the local 0-3.3V logic boundary.

vsysDmmVolts.procedure: Measure VSYS-to-GND before attaching the Pico; use the DMM 6V DC range when available.

gpioLogicVolts.procedure: Probe GP2/GP3/GP6/GP7/GP8 only relative to local GND.

adcPinVolts.procedure: Never drive GP26 above ADC_VREF; the external divider maps 0-5.5V VSYS to at most 2.89V with the specified 5% resistors.

scope.procedure: Use 1x/10x probe only on local low-voltage nodes; no mains or product rails.

continuityAndResistance.procedure: De-energize and disconnect USB before resistance or continuity checks.

evidenceCapture.usbPoweredSetup: Use the Pico micro-USB and FTDI logger only for programming, normal button/UI cases and reset-cause serial logs. FTDI VCC remains physically disconnected.
evidenceCapture.directVsysCases: For B9/B10 brownout and power-loss cases, unplug Pico USB and the FTDI USB cable at both ends. Capture the direct-VSYS voltage/current waveform and supply record with DMM/scope. If a reset-cause log is needed, run the identical scripted case separately in the USB-powered setup and label it USB-powered; never present it as direct-VSYS evidence.
evidenceCapture.requiredSeparation: Serial logs and direct-VSYS waveforms are separate sequential evidence. No USB VBUS, UART VCC, display power or instrument lead may create a second source during direct-VSYS tests.

buildSequence: Inventory parts and mark a separate LOW-SPEED BENCH area; reject any USB-C, dock, target laptop or product-power item.
Inspect the Pico order code and headers; install it across the breadboard center gap.
Program firmware through Pico micro-USB; confirm boot/reset logging; disconnect USB at both ends.
With the Pico disconnected, measure micro-USB VBUS to local GND and record 0V before VSYS wiring.
Set the supply to 3.3V, 100mA current limit, output off; verify with DMM; connect only VSYS and GND.
Add and test GP2 local button, then add UART logger with VCC omitted; prove inactive outputs and event logs.
Add the display and LED through their resistors; use diagnostic labels only.
Add the GP26 divider and capacitor; calibrate ADC readings against the DMM across 0-5.5V only.
Add the second request button locally on the breadboard; test open, clean press, bounce and short-to-ground at the current limit; do not attach a remote cable.
Capture raw serial logs, current/voltage notes, reset causes and wiring photo; leave USB disconnected for direct-VSYS evidence.

ownerChecklist.action: Locate or approve one exact Pico 2 board: SC1631 default or SC1632 with headers.
Confirm a single-output current-limited supply can be set to 3.3V and <=100mA; do not buy a supply until checking existing equipment.
Confirm a DMM with a 6V DC range or better, test leads and continuity/resistance mode.
Confirm breadboard, 28AWG jumpers, two dry-contact buttons, passives and a 3.3V-safe display.
Confirm a 3.3V UART logger; if buying, use FTDI TTL-232R-3V3 and leave its VCC pin disconnected.
Confirm that the base build has no remote cable; any TVS and remote-cable plan requires independent review before connection.
Re-open each manufacturer and authorized-distributor URL and record current stock, exact order code, price, shipping and tax before asking for purchase approval.
After approval, acquire traceable parts; record received MPN, date code/lot where present, and actual quantities. Do not substitute silently.
